newsitem.title: USA: Edison Brothers files reorganization plan.
newsitem.headline: Edison Brothers files reorganization plan.

text.p: Edison Brothers Stores Inc said Thursday it filed its plan of Chapter 11 bankruptcy reorganization.
The company has been under bankruptcy protection since November 3, 1995.

Under terms of the plan, creditors would receive $119 million in cash, $100 million in 10-year, 11-percent unsecured notes, and new Edison common stock to be issued at the time of emergence from bankruptcy and replacing all existing shares, the retailer said.
Creditors would also receive title to the company's St. Louis headquarters building, which Edison would continue to occupy under the terms of a 10-year lease.
Creditors would also receive about $40 million in cash from the company's overfunded pension plan, the retailer said.
Shareholders would receive warrants entitling them to buy up to nine percent of the new stock at pre-determined prices, Edison Brothers said.
The plan, geared toward satisfying $440 million in creditor claims, is subject to approval by the court, creditors and shareholders, the company said.

"The plan we filed today will allow Edison to emerge from Chapter 11 as a stronger specialty retailer," said Alan Miller, chairman and president of the company. "Edison has used the Chapter 11 process to stabilize its business and establish a solid foundation on which to build the future."
